definition: A decision by Employment and Social Development Canada on whether hiring a foreign national for a specific Canadian job would have a positive, neutral or negative effect on the Canadian labour market. The employer applies for it, not the worker.
longform: A positive LMIA is required before most employer-sponsored work permits and says nothing about the worker's own qualifications or admissibility — it is a judgement about one position at one employer. A positive assessment issued on an application received on or after 1 May 2024 is valid for a maximum of 6 months, inside which the named worker must apply for their work permit.
